name: New Jersey
nameStory: Named for the Isle of Jersey, a small island in the English Channel that Sir George Carteret had defended for the king. He was handed a chunk of America as a reward and named it after his island - so the most crowded state in the country is named for a rock off the coast of France.
capitalStory: Trenton is simply 'Trent's town,' after a merchant. Its real significance is one night: December 26, 1776, when Washington crossed the ice-choked Delaware and captured the Hessian garrison here. The Revolution was collapsing, and Trenton is where it turned around.

majorFeatures.name: Pine Barrens
majorFeatures.note: A million acres of wilderness in the densest state

majorFeatures.name: Appalachian Ridges
majorFeatures.note: Folded ridges in the northwest corner

funFacts: New Jersey is the most densely populated state in the country.
'Garden State' is literal: it grew fruit and vegetables for the two huge cities on either side of it, New York and Philadelphia.
The Pine Barrens sit on top of a vast clean aquifer, and are so undeveloped that people got lost in them for centuries.
About 100 battles and skirmishes of the Revolution were fought in New Jersey - more than in any other state.
